item.text:
**6B.8 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed (2024)**

**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning no. I found real 2024 evidence of inclusion-oriented policy in education, refugee ID access, GBV services, and some gender-sensitive consultation. But the dominant 2024 record is still coercive: emergency-law detention, forced evictions, ethnic arrests, refugee detention, and heavy restrictions on speech and assembly. I did not find strong direct 2024 evidence that Abiy consistently kept jobs, permits, housing, or benefits insulated from political control.

**Positive / mitigating evidence**
- **Building a Strong Foundation to Improve Learning Outcomes in Ethiopia** - World Bank, 2024-09-05. URL: [worldbank.org](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia). Claim: GEQIP-E expanded girls’ enrollment in historically disadvantaged regions, supported students with special needs, and integrated refugee schools into the national system. This is evidence for equal opportunity in education, not just aggregate enrollment gains. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **Gender-based Violence (GBV) Response Services in Ethiopia: Empowering Women and Girls in Conflict-Affected Areas** - World Bank, 2024-10-11. URL: [worldbank.org](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/10/11/gender-based-violence-gbv-response-services-in-afe-ethiopia-empowering-women-and-girls-in-conflict-affected-areas). Claim: the government-backed project expanded GBV response across five conflict-affected regions and explicitly targeted women and girls. This supports dignity-centered service delivery in a high-risk setting. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.6, 6B.7.
- **Unlocking opportunities for refugees** - World Bank, 2024-06-30. URL: [worldbank.org](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/30/unlocking-opportunities-for-refugees). Claim: Ethiopia’s Fayda ID rollout was designed to include nearly one million refugees and improve access to essential services, while easing tensions and promoting belonging. This is one of the clearest equal-opportunity signals in the record. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services** - UNHCR Africa, 2024-03-07. URL: [unhcr.org](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services). Claim: the government and UNHCR launched a refugee ID initiative to facilitate access to basic services. This is direct inclusion evidence for refugees and asylum seekers. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **UN Women supports Civil Society Organizations’ engagement in transitional justice policy** - United Nations in Ethiopia, 2024-09-09. URL: [ethiopia.un.org](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/283986-un-women-supports-civil-society-organizations%E2%80%99-engagement-transitional-justice-policy). Claim: women leaders and grassroots groups were brought into transitional-justice implementation work, with an explicit goal of gender sensitivity and women’s participation. This is a meaningful inclusion signal, though it is consultation rather than proof of durable equal power. Question IDs: 6B.8.

**Negative evidence**
- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** - Human Rights Watch, 2024. URL: [hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia). Claim: HRW reported forced evictions near Addis Ababa, mass arrests of ethnic Amharas, journalist arrests, and arbitrary detention of refugees and asylum seekers. This points strongly against equal dignity and non-discriminatory treatment. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6, 6B.3.
- **Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent** - Amnesty International, 2024-02-19. URL: [amnesty.org](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/). Claim: emergency powers were used to detain critics and journalists, restrict movement, and ban assemblies and associations. That is punitive control, not equal civic standing. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law** - Amnesty International, 2024-10-01. URL: [amnesty.org](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/). Claim: authorities detained hundreds of civilians without warrants or timely court appearance. This is strong evidence of coercive punishment rather than dignity-preserving governance. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region** - Amnesty International, 2024-11-06. URL: [amnesty.org](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/). Claim: a joint task force filled makeshift detention camps with thousands of civilians, and Amnesty said mass detention had become a routine political tool. This is strong evidence against equal treatment and against non-punitive administration. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.7, 6B.6.
- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** - Human Rights Watch, 2024. URL: [hrw.org](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region). Claim: federal forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi. This is direct evidence that civilians in crisis zones were not being protected with equal dignity. Question IDs: 6B.8, also 6B.6, 6B.3.

**Search gap**
- I found little direct 2024 evidence on the most specific part of this lens, namely whether Abiy used **jobs, permits, or housing** as routine loyalty rewards or punishments. The strongest evidence instead came from adjacent behaviors: emergency detention, forced evictions, aid diversion, refugee exclusion, and censorship. That means the conclusion rests more on patterns of coercion and unequal treatment than on a clean paper trail for patronage-by-permit or patronage-by-job.
